(1) we present a novel utility accrual scheduling criterion that allows a task's utility to be specified as a function of other task's completion times and their progress, and (2) our experimental results with a POSIX RTOS implementation of a scheduling algorithm for this criterion show that the criterion is effective in applications that require a task's utility be dependent on the completion times of multiple other tasks
we have developed a utility accrual model that is more flexible and generalizes the previous model.

In summary, our research is concerned with
extending the time/utility theory of scheduling to accommodate joint utility functions and progressive utility.
the development of a new scheduling criterion and the corresponding algorithm for the scheduling of activities that accrue utility over time.
the scheduling of activities with utility accrual functions that depend on the progress of other activities, in addition to the progress of the activity being scheduled.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a utility accrual scheduling framework that allows the modeling and scheduling of activities with joint utilities.

we are able to provide a more complete and accurate description of the utility of activities, and that we can provide an algorithm for scheduling under this model that is both effective and practical.
the CUA algorithm provides a practical approach for scheduling activities in the presence of joint utility functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have extended the utility accrual model to include joint utility functions and we have presented an algorithm that can be used to maximize the weighted sum of joint, progressive, and completion time utilities for a set of activities with joint utility functions.
we have developed a new utility accrual scheduling algorithm for the class of applications that can benefit from joint utility functions.
we have developed a general model for utility accrual scheduling that can be applied to a wide range of utility accrual scheduling problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the joint utility functions can be used to model utility accrual for a class of applications that have been previously studied using imprecise utility functions.
the concept of joint utilities can be used to capture the utility accrual of an activity as a function of other activities' progress.
JUFs can be used to model a wide range of scheduling applications that require utility functions to be a function of other activities' completion times and progress.
